summary: From 1978 to 1994 Arkansas prisons sold inmates' blood plasma through politically connected for-profit contractors with lax screening and reused needles, exporting hepatitis- and HIV-tainted plasma that infected thousands in Canada and Britain.
keywords: Factor 8: The Arkansas Prison Blood Scandal

evidence.note: Clinton takes office as governor in 1978 just as the prison plasma program is about to start
Henderson's firm becomes HMA in 1978 and wins the contract for all prison medicine and plasma
contractor reuses needles on donors to save costs, spreading infection inside the prison
plasma sold via a Montreal broker that hid its prison origin from foreign buyers
Clinton places HMA's head and its attorney in state posts tied to the prison system
legislators controlling the prisons block reform and shield the program from Clinton
British hemophiliac brothers infected with HIV, one dies in 1986 amid mob harassment
Pine Bluff Biological Products takes over the plasma contract as an insider deal
a New York firm runs the program from 1991 until it ends in 1994; Canadian death toll
Canadian Red Cross collapses and a 1995 federal commission traces blood back to Cummins
tainted US factor concentrate drives the worst treatment disaster in NHS history
host weighs and largely dismisses Vince Foster and Clinton cover-up theories

notes: No theme for the blood or plasma trade; public-health is closest. Clinton kept secondary as the story frames him as an enabler, not the subject. Pre-1978 material (history of transfusion, 1960s paid-donor research, 1974 blood policy, 1982 FDA request) treated as background, so covered_span starts with the program. The 2000s documentary segment is an epilogue, not a reason for reaches_present.
